Debrecen Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Debrecen, Hungary

Not demolished. Jewish merchants first arrived in Debrecen in the 1780s, though Jews were barred from settling there - or even staying overnight - until 1840; early residents lived around Hatvan Street, founding a burial society in 1844 and formal community in 1852. When the community applied to establish this cemetery in 1842, city authorities initially resisted permitting a stone fence around it, since - unusually for the era - Christian cemeteries in the city went unfenced; the cemetery was ultimately placed on Monostorpályi Road, in an area outside town deemed unsuitable for building or farming. The community grew to support multiple synagogues (three built during its 'Golden Age' before WWI, two still standing today), a Jewish school, grammar school, mikveh, hospital, and social services. Of 9,142 Jews recorded in 1941, only 3,306 remained by April 1944 (598 taxpayers, 25 community employees); over 6,000 Debrecen-area Jews died in the Holocaust. Survivors largely emigrated to Israel, the US, or Budapest, leaving today's community less than a tenth its prewar size. This cemetery, allegedly founded in the 1840s, remains active today with about 9,000 tombstones - the largest single cemetery in this dataset.
